new.title: See the world's largest cathedral organ in Dom St. Stephan
new.desc: Dom St. Stephan is the baroque landmark of the old town, rebuilt after the fire of 1662 with Carlo Lurago as the leading architect. Its organ, completed in 1928 and since expanded, is counted as the largest cathedral organ in the world.
new.tip: Free to enter outside services; the organ is played in scheduled concerts, see the Dommusik programme. Look up at the stucco ceiling.

new.title: Explore Veste Oberhaus above the three rivers
new.desc: Veste Oberhaus was founded in 1219 by Bishop Ulrich II and grew into one of Europe's largest surviving castle complexes. It houses the Oberhausmuseum and has an observation tower over the old town and the river confluence.
new.tip: Open mid-March to mid-November (check hours); a lift runs from the visitor car park, or walk up via the Ludwigsteig in about 15 minutes.

new.title: Watch three rivers meet at the Dreiflüsseeck
new.desc: At the Ortspitze the blue Inn and the dark Ilz join the green Danube, often with a visible colour line. The tip of the peninsula is a public park with a view of Veste Oberhaus.
new.tip: Best on a clear morning when the colours contrast. Free, with benches and a riverside walk.

new.title: Visit the Altstädter Rathaus and its flood marks
new.desc: The Rathaus on Rathausplatz is a Gothic town hall expanded in the 19th century with a tower and a glockenspiel. Marks on its wall record the great Danube floods of past centuries.
new.tip: The glockenspiel plays daily at 11:30 and 14:30 according to the tourist office, which sits in the same building.

new.title: Walk to the Schaiblingsturm on the Inn
new.desc: The Schaiblingsturm is a medieval round defensive tower on the bank of the Inn, part of the old town fortifications. It stands along the Innpromenade with a view across to the Innstadt.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll along the Innpromenade; the tower is viewed from outside. Pleasant at sunset.

new.title: See the frescoes at Kloster Niedernburg
new.desc: Niedernburg Abbey is one of the oldest in Bavaria, and its church holds the tomb of Gisela of Bavaria. The Fresko-Museum preserves frescoes recalling St. Mary's church, destroyed in the town fires of the 17th century.
new.tip: Check opening hours of the Fresken-Museum at the tourist office. The abbey lies near the tip of the peninsula.

new.title: Step back to Rome at Kastell Boiotro
new.desc: The Roman museum in the Innstadt sits on the foundations of the late Roman fort Boiotro, in a late medieval house. It shows finds from the Roman frontier on the Danube.
new.tip: Small museum, about an hour; the Innstadt is quieter than the old town. Check seasonal opening hours.

new.title: Browse modern art at Museum Moderner Kunst Wörlen
new.desc: The museum is based on the estate of the painter Georg Philipp Wörlen (1886-1954) and shows 20th and 21st century art. It runs about ten temporary exhibitions a year.
new.tip: Look up the current exhibition before going. Good for a rainy afternoon.
new.q: Museum Moderner Kunst Wörlen, Bräugasse 17, 94032 Passau

new.title: Marvel at Bohemian glass in the Glasmuseum Passau
new.desc: The Glasmuseum in the Hotel Wilder Mann occupies several historic patrician houses on the Danube. It is described as the largest museum of European glass, with a focus on Bohemian glass.
new.tip: Plan about 1.5 hours; the entrance is at Rathausplatz.

new.title: See church treasures at the Museum am Dom
new.desc: The Museum am Dom is in the Residence building next to the cathedral and shows art masterpieces and treasures of the Passau diocese.
new.tip: Check opening days, which vary by season; combine with a visit to the cathedral next door.

new.title: Stroll Residenzplatz and the Neue Residenz
new.desc: Residenzplatz lies beside the cathedral and is framed by the Baroque and Rococo bishop's residence. It is one of the old town's most photographed squares.
new.tip: Best seen in the morning light; free to walk through.

new.title: Step inside Studienkirche St. Michael
new.desc: The Jesuit Studienkirche St. Michael is a Baroque church built in the 17th century with rich stucco. It is also a venue of the Europäische Wochen festival.
new.tip: Usually open to visitors during the day; check for concert times.

new.title: Drink a Hacklberger beer at the Bräustüberl
new.desc: The Hacklberger Bräustüberl is the brewery tavern of Brauerei Hacklberg, whose brewing dates to 1618. It has a large beer garden that moves indoors in winter and a kitchen serving regional dishes.
new.tip: Try a Hacklberger Hell with a Schweinsbraten. The beer garden is the draw in summer.

new.title: Taste estate wine at the Heilig-Geist-Stiftsschenke
new.desc: This historic wine tavern dates to 1358 and belongs to the Heilig-Geist hospital foundation, with a rustic Stiftskeller. It serves estate wines and fresh fish.
new.tip: Order a glass of the Stift's own wine with the fish of the day.

new.title: Try the Passauer Goldhaube at Café Simon
new.desc: Café Simon on Rindermarkt began in 1903 as a wax chandler, confectioner and gingerbread maker and still sits in its original rooms. It is known for chocolates and its Passauer Goldhaube specialty.
new.tip: Take a Goldhaube or a slice of cake with coffee; it closes earlier than the restaurants.

new.title: Eat Bavarian classics at the Peschl-Terrasse
new.desc: The Peschl-Terrasse near the Roßtränke is a brewery restaurant with a terrace, in the same family since 1855, serving beer from Peschl's own brewery.
new.tip: Listed as open daily from 11:00; try a Hell with a Bavarian main on the terrace.

new.title: Order a Weißbier at Wirtshaus Andorfer
new.desc: The Gasthof Weissbräu Andorfer is a wheat-beer inn at Rennweg, serving Bavarian specialties with a warm kitchen all day.
new.tip: Try the house Weißbier with a Schweinshaxe; Veste Oberhaus is close by.

new.title: Dine at the Wirtshaus Altes Bräuhaus by the bridge
new.desc: The Wirtshaus Altes Bräuhaus serves regional cuisine on Bräugasse by the suspension bridge, with a view of Veste Oberhaus.
new.tip: Ask for a table with a view; order a regional Bavarian dish such as Krustenbraten.

new.title: Eat fish at Restaurant Pomeranz
new.desc: Pomeranz is a Mediterranean restaurant in the Bratfischwinkel lane by the Inn where fish dishes are especially popular.
new.tip: Order the fish of the day; reserve for dinner in summer.

new.title: Have coffee at KaffeeWerk in the Innstadt
new.desc: KaffeeWerk is a café just across the Marienbrücke in the Innstadt, away from the tourist crowds, with seating for 30 inside and 60 on the terrace.
new.tip: Order a coffee and cake on the terrace; a good stop after the Mariahilf climb.

new.title: Eat grilled chicken at the Hendlhouse
new.desc: The Hendlhouse on Große Klingergasse serves hearty Bavarian food, mainly grilled poultry.
new.tip: Order the half Hendl with a Radler; casual and good value.

new.title: Cruise the three rivers on the Dreiflüsse-Rundfahrt
new.desc: The Dreiflüsse-Stadtrundfahrt starts at the landing at Rathausplatz and sails past the old town and the confluence of Danube, Inn and Ilz. It runs from late March to early November.
new.tip: Check departure times with the operator; the upper deck gives the best photos of the peninsula.

new.title: Follow the night watchman Lindl through the alleys
new.desc: Passau Tourism offers a lantern-lit tour with the night watchman Lindl, who tells of his hard work and picks a helper from the group.
new.tip: Book via the tourist information at Rathausplatz; dates are seasonal.

new.title: Climb the Ludwigsteig up to Veste Oberhaus
new.desc: The Ludwigsteig and the Wehrgang along the castle walls take about 15 minutes uphill, with views of the old town. An alternative entry starts at Angerstraße (about 20 minutes).
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; the lift from the car park is the easier route.

new.title: Climb the 321 steps to Mariahilf
new.desc: The pilgrimage church Mariahilf sits above the Innstadt, reached by a covered stairway of 321 steps lined with votive tablets. Entry is free.
new.tip: Go in the morning; the view of the old town from the top is worth it.

new.title: Cycle the Innpromenade and the Donauradweg start
new.desc: Passau is the starting point of the Austrian Donauradweg (about 380 km to Vienna) and a stop on the Innradweg. The Innpromenade starts near the station and follows the river upstream.
new.tip: Rent a touring bike or e-bike at a shop in the old town; the flat riverside path suits easy rides.

new.title: Join the Maidult at Messepark Kohlbruck
new.desc: The Passauer Maidult is a spring beer festival with tents, a costume parade and fireworks. The 2026 edition ran from 30 April to 10 May.
new.tip: Held each spring; check the Passauer Dult website for exact 2027 dates.

new.title: Attend a concert of the Europäische Wochen
new.desc: The Festspiele Europäische Wochen Passau run from late June to late July, with around 50 events in about 30 venues, including open-air concerts at the Ortspitze.
new.tip: Book tickets early via ew-passau.de; the 2026 edition ran from 20 June to 26 July.

new.title: Walk the Ilzstadt to the Ilz
new.desc: The Ilzstadt is the quieter Ilz-side district under Veste Oberhaus, where the dark Ilz flows into the Danube. Hiking routes from Passau follow the Ilz upstream.
new.tip: Wear comfortable shoes; start from the Ortspitze and walk through the Ilzstadt.
